payload.name: Preserve prior specifics when enriching memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory, use this if the new content is more general, emotional, or abstract than the stored fact, or if the update would drop previously captured details.
content: During CRUD, before updating or merging an existing memory, compare the new content against the stored facts. Preserve every specific, time-bound fact already captured (e.g., doctor visits, diagnoses, dates, locations) unless directly contradicted by new evidence.

If new messages add broader context such as general struggles, feelings, or quotes about the same topic, do not replace the concrete earlier fact with that framing. Create an enriched version that keeps the old specifics and appends the new nuance.

If an update would remove a previously captured fact that is not contradicted, treat the update as a loss: retain the old detail and add the new information instead. Stop once the memory contains both the preserved facts and the relevant new context; do not expand into unrelated details.

solves: During CRUD, an existing memory that contains a concrete, time-bound fact is sometimes overwritten by a later, more general summary that drops the fact, making it impossible to answer future questions about the specific event. This Skill ensures updates preserve previously stored specifics while incorporating new context.
